I'm good with this position.  Using optional for all of them is a lot more clumsy. 

There is a subtle case where this generated code is more likely to crash (actually, throw an exception) but any case of it is a server-side bug that we should really fix anyhow: enums.

Enums aren't a first-class concept in dbus, but they are in sdbusplus.  What we do is generate fully qualified strings (ie. `xyz.openbmc_project.Interface.EnumType.EnumValue`) and that's what we send across dbus, but when they are pulled out of the message they are converted into a C++ enum.  If the conversion fails, it throws an exception.

Two possibilities with the code you have:
1. `get_all_properties<variant<enum, string>>` -- The enum conversion may fail, which will devolve into a string.  Your visit function will see the wrong type and skip the property.
2. `get_all_properties<variant<enum>>` -- The enum conversion may fail and will throw an exception because there is no other obvious type to convert to.

I don't think a change is necessary, but up to you.  Right now your visit checks type and then name.  If we switch to name and then type we could report condition #1 rather than devolving to the default value (because the property name will match but the expected vs received type will not match).

I've inverted the loop and will now report the type mismatch via a suitable thrown exception. I didn't realize that exceptions were the way here, so now I think it makes more sense.

Are you guaranteed to try to interpret/unpack as the enum first? If yes, then the failure will now be caught (see your other suggestion). If no, then isn't there is a concern that the type would be unpacked as a string, then *incorrectly* throw an exception?

Looking at the read code, I believe this is a bit broken and may throw invalid exceptions if there is an enum type present. I think that we need to do the following:

1) Omit the enum types from the variants during decode
2) Perform the enum type conversion at name matching instead

This is a bunch of template magic that I'm happy to have you land afterwards if you feel comfortable with that, but wanted to check my understanding.

I think this works as-is right now.

https://github.com/openbmc/sdbusplus/blob/56dd6dd45837670e8cce56a0602e6dfe5dc75816/include/sdbusplus/message/read.hpp#L389
https://github.com/openbmc/sdbusplus/blob/56dd6dd45837670e8cce56a0602e6dfe5dc75816/include/sdbusplus/message/native_types.hpp#L240

The first one is a specialization for `read_single<variant>`.  This identifies if the variant type is either a string or an enum (when decoding) and delegates it to another function (`convert_from_string`).

The second one is the `convert_from_string` implementation for variants.  It iterates through all the types, trying the enums first and then falling back to the string.  (If the variant only had enums, it ends up returning an empty `optional`, which the `read` function turns into an exception.)

Got it. I think it works sufficiently well as long as the enum types are namespaced & mostly exclusive with string values, which AFAICT *should* be generally true but is not formally guaranteed. It breaks only if you want to send a string which happens to exactly match the fully-namespaced enum name (https://github.com/openbmc/sdbusplus/blob/56dd6dd45837670e8cce56a0602e6dfe5dc75816/tools/sdbusplus/templates/interface.common.hpp.mako#L116). Enums can't collide because they would collide in C++ as well.

I actually think this can be trivially hanlded by just restoring the string if the type is a string and it matches `has_convert_from_string`. I've added this code, and I think now all types should be handled just fine.

> I actually think this can be trivially hanlded by just restoring the string if the type is a string and it matches has_convert_from_string. I've added this code, and I think now all types should be handled just fine.

Why do we need this code now?  It isn't clear to me that it adds value over what already exists in the underlying `read` support.

The read will try to resolve each Enum in the variant first (makes sense). But if you want to send the string "xyz.openbmc_project.Interface.EnumType.EnumValue" and it happens to match with an existing Enum, even if happens to correspond to a string property, it will try to decoded as the Enum variant.

This code is just undoing that if necessary, e.g. if you want a string and see something that was decoded from a string on the wire (i.e. an Enum), then just undoes that a saves the property as a strong.

If this edge case is too esoteric then I can roll it back, but hopefully we're on the same page about the case it is handling.

> This code is just undoing that if necessary, e.g. if you want a string and see something that was decoded from a string on the wire (i.e. an Enum), then just undoes that a saves the property as a strong.

Oh.  Understood.

> If this edge case is too esoteric then I can roll it back, but hopefully we're on the same page about the case it is handling.

Yeah, let's just drop it.  That's not really supported in the base read code either.  The enum strings are purposefully encoded in a way that this shouldn't be a real use-case.  If someone has a string-that-looks-like-an-enum-but-isn't, they probably have a bug in their interface design anyhow.  (We almost never allow raw strings that are programmatically interpreted, rather than intended for humans)

In theory we could use the default value in the property as the sane-default in the struct.

This method could be lifted up into the `property` class and then called similarly as `property = default;` in the struct definition: https://github.com/openbmc/sdbusplus/blob/56dd6dd45837670e8cce56a0602e6dfe5dc75816/tools/sdbusplus/templates/property.aserver.value.hpp.mako#L5
Done. That method was duplicated a bit, I've lifted it and removed that specific template, since it seems simpler without it.

Thanks.  This is great.

There is some behavior where we can use `sdbusplus::async::client<T1, T2>` to make a single proxy of both interfaces, which isn't covered by this code, but I think this is a good enough start.  I can refactor later on to support the `client<...>` case.

Have a few minor comments.

I don't know if you've used `clang-format` against the generated code.  It's almost impossible to get generated code to not change against `clang-format` but I try to make the template.mako files as close to the `clang-format` output as possible.  I don't recall of off hand if the lambda formatting you used matches the default format we use.

Much appreciated that the complex case can be deferred.

I've made the output match clang-format perfectly for the example. No guarantees otherwise (and it was already a bit off in other parts, e.g. headers and constructor), but hopefully that's good for this change.
Ok if we do `properties_t`?

```suggestion
        return proxy.template get_all_properties<PropertiesVariant>(context()) |
```

We already generate PropertiesVariant, which you'll want to use here.  The existing PropertiesVariant uses some template magic to deduplicate the types otherwise you can end up with `variant<foo, foo, ...>` which doesn't compile.
Perfect. Done.
